A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for a full-rank channel, we show that a source is resolvable if and only if it can be used to generate a random number sequence that can be used to approximately generate the channel's output for any input.
we show that the resolvability and the separation between source coding and channel coding can be extended from the deterministic case to the random case.

we have shown that a given source can approximate any given channel if and only if the source can be separated from the channel in the sense that the random number generation (RNG) capacity and the resolvability capacity are both positive.

for the case of full-rank channels, we can separate random number generation (RNG) and resolvability (RSL) problems.
